subject: OrbitAI: follow-up & proposed latency/throughput A/B tests
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Thompson <alex.thompson@orbitai.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 17:12:00 -0700
Subject: OrbitAI: follow-up & proposed latency/throughput A/B tests

Alex — great to meet earlier. Quick recap + concrete next steps so we keep momentum: 

Call recap (30m)
- Primary use: interactive customer-facing summarization at OrbitAI (avg. request ~600 tokens).
- Success metrics: p95 latency < 250ms for single-turn queries, p99 < 350ms for peak; sustained tokens/sec targets for batch re-rank jobs.
- Competitive concern: you saw regressions on other managed inference APIs at high concurrency; want to validate in your environment.

What we propose
1) Two-arm A/B benchmark comparing (A) Redwood hosted inference (Redwood-3B-quant / Redwood-7B-fp16) vs (B) Hyperscaler-managed endpoint your team is testing (you mentioned Vertex endpoints).
2) Run targeted scenarios: low-latency single-turn (concurrency sweep 1-8), bursty traffic (100-500 rps at short windows), and batch throughput (4k token batches).
3) Measure: p50/p90/p95/p99 latencies, tokens/sec, tail latency variance, error rates, and cost-per-1M tokens.

Deliverables we’ll provide
- Benchmark plan (.csv) with payloads and concurrency matrix (attached: benchmark-plan-v1.csv).
- Lightweight load harness & instrumentation script to run from your GCP test subnet (attached: redwood-harness.sh).
- Short results dashboard + trace links once tests complete.

Next steps / asks
- Can you add Samir (infra) to the thread so we can coordinate a test subnet + test keys?
- Approval to run 3 x 15-minute test windows in your dev project next Tuesday (May 11) or anytime that week.
- Any redlines on the payloads attached (benchmark-plan-v1.csv) — we can replace synthetic prompts with a scrubbed sample of your traffic.

Attachments: 20270503-orbitai-discovery-notes.pdf (PDF), benchmark-plan-v1.csv (CSV), redwood-harness.sh (shell script stub)

Thanks — talk soon,

Marissa Cole

Subject: RE: OrbitAI: follow-up & proposed latency/throughput A/B tests

Alex / Samir — looping in the technical approach below so you have an operational view. Happy to run a dry run with your infra team beforehand.

Test harness (high level)
- Runner: lightweight k6 + wrapper script (we’ll provide Docker image). attached redwood-harness.sh is a shim that hits both endpoints and records histograms.
- Endpoints:
  - Redwood hosted: https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate (api keys we’ll exchange securely)
  - Hyperscaler-managed endpoint: your vertex URL (we’ll hit whatever endpoint Samir provides)
- Payloads: 3 collections (short interactive ~100–400 tokens, medium ~400–1k, long batch >2k).
- Concurrency matrix: [1,2,4,8] for single-turn tests; burst tests use ramp to 250–500rps for 30s windows; batch throughput uses 8 concurrent workers with 4k-token batches.

Metrics & instrumentation
- Capture p50/p90/p95/p99 latency (client-side) + server-side traces if we can hook OpenTelemetry.
- Record tokens/sec, CPU/GPU utilization (if you expose), and 95th pct tail-bandwidth.
- Cost calc: token charges + estimated infra time (we’ll export per-run totals).

Model variants + fairness note
- We recommend testing both quantized medium models (to simulate lowest-cost baseline) and fp16 larger variants to observe tail-latency tradeoffs.
- We’ll mark any run that exhibits >0.5% error rate or >2x p99 variance for deeper investigation.

Logistics / security
- Send an API key specifically for these runs (scoped, short TTL), or we can generate ephemeral keys if you prefer.
- We will not store raw prompts longer than 30 days; results dashboard will contain aggregated metrics only.

I’ll post the runner image and a short runbook to the shared Drive link shortly. If Samir can provide the Vertex endpoint + test VPC details by EOD Friday, we’ll be set to run Monday/Tuesday next week.

— Rishi

If anything changes on your side, flag it in-thread so we don’t lose context. Looking forward — will have the Drive artifacts and a short slide deck ready post-run.
